How would the medication work when the person was poorly nourished, had weak immunity and did not know where the next meal would come from? This was a question Randall often raised with his doctor friend Nikhil Dhanpal, who remembers him as someone who looked beyond a patient's illness to understand the conditions in which they lived. For Randall, healthcare was much more than hospitals, medicines and doctors. It was about access to food, forests, land and livelihoods for the communities he served. This approach shaped his work among tribal villages in Odisha's Kalahandi district, where he moved to in 2017. Over the years, his work as a doctor brought him closer to the impact of mining on community health and to the anti-mining movement in the Sijimali hills. Since July 2023, villagers in the bauxite-capped Sijimali hill range, located along the Kalahandi-Rayagada border in southern Odisha, have been actively opposing a mining project, demanding cancellation of lease given to Vedanta Limited. items.title: Umar Khalid moves Supreme Court seeking bail in Delhi riots conspiracy case
items.summary: Former Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) scholar and Delhi riots conspiracy case accused Umar Khalid has moved the Supreme Court seeking bail in the case. He has challenged the September 30 order of the Delhi High Court denying him bail. The Delhi High Court had observed that the Supreme Court had denied bail to Khalid and Imam in January 2026, stating that they can file for bail again after a year or after the protected witnesses have been examined. The High Court said that since the two conditions have not been met yet, granting bail to Khalid and Imam would amount to modifying the Supreme Court order, which the High Court cannot do. “In view of the above discussion and overall facts of these cases, specifically the conditions imposed by the Supreme Court in Gulfisha Fatima, this court cannot find fault with the order passed by the trial court. The present appeals are therefore dismissed,” the court said. This is the second time Khalid is approaching the Supreme Court seeking bail. The most recent order of the top court came in January 2026 when five people were granted bail, but Khalid and Imam were declined relief . He then once again moved the trial court which rejected his pleas on July 4 . Subsequently, the High Court rejected his plea on September 30. Notably, Khalid's bail plea before the High Court relied on the Supreme Court's judgment in a different case of Syed Iftikhar Andrabi wherein a different bench of the top court questioned the apex court's denial of bail to him and Imam in the January 2026 verdict. Khalid had argued that the same amounts to a change in circumstances. However, the police countered that the judgment of a coordinate bench in a different case cannot override the specific findings and directions passed by the Supreme Court in Khalid and Imam's own case. The High Court proceeded to reject Khalid's plea prompting him to file the present plea before the apex court.

items.title: Bombay High Court cancels bail granted to ex-cop Sachin Waze in Antilia bomb scare case
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Thursday cancelled the bail granted to former Mumbai Police officer Sachin Waze in the 2021 Antilia bomb scare and Mansukh Hiren murder case. [National Investigation Agency v. State of Maharashtra & Anr.] A division bench of Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale pronounced the verdict on an appeal filed by the NIA challenging the bail granted by a special court on September 29. A detailed order is awaited. Justices GS Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale The special court had questioned the applicability of terrorism charges under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against Waze afyer noting lack of witness statements from the Ambani family. In appeal before the High Court, Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh argued on behalf of NIA that the special judge passed an erroneous order. He pointed out that statements from Antilia's security personnel had indeed been recorded. former ASG Anil Singh He argued that Waze parked the gelatin-laden SUV outside Mukesh Ambani’s residence for extortion and to stage-manage a terror plot, hoping to solve it and project himself as a supercop. When vehicle owner Mansukh Hiren refused to take the fall, he was allegedly eliminated as a weak link. Senior Advocate VM Thorat representing Waze, countered that even if the NIA's narrative is accepted, staging a scare merely to regain his clout does not constitute terrorism under Section 15 of the UAPA. He argued that intimidating a single family using gelatin sticks without a detonator does not strike terror in the general public, adding that eliminating Hiren amounted to destruction of evidence rather than a terror act. Thorat also pressed for bail citing Waze's five-year incarceration and parity with co-accused. After considering the arguments, the Court today cancelled the bail. The ASG along with advocates Chintan Shah, Amogh Singh and Adarsh Vyas appeared for NIA. Throat and advocates Sajal Yadav, Shalabh Saxena, Aarti Kalekar, Harsh Ghangurde, Raj Raut, Aayushya Geruja, Nihal Rebello, Rasheed Lakhwa and Disha Hatkar represented Waze.

In the interim order passed today, Justice Jamdar has restrained various entities from exploiting Panday's personality attributes or passing off goods and services as being endorsed by her. items.summary: The Allahabad High Court on Thursday rejected a plea seeking the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi in relation to the remarks made by him about religious freedom in India, in relation to the Sikh community [Nageshwar Mishra and another v State of UP and another] Justice Vikram D Chauhan noted that Gandhi had said that there is an atmosphere of insecurity among Sikhs in India. items.title: Centre supports plea in Supreme Court to deny post-resignation perks to tainted constitutional functionaries
items.summary: The Central government on Thursday told the Supreme Court that the public interest litigation (PIL) seeking to deny post-resignation perks and amenities to constitutional functionaries, including judges, who quit to avoid removal proceedings, appeared to have merit [Pratik Vira v Union of India] . Solicitor General Tushar Mehta , appearing for the Central government, acknowledged before a Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that the petitioner, one Pratik Vira, appeared to have made out a case. He then undertook to obtain instructions and file a response. The Court, subsequently, allowed an intervention application and directed the Union government to file its counter-affidavit. CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi Earlier, the plea had come up before the Supreme Court on September 3. The Court had sought the response of the Central government then. The petitioner moved the Court arguing that constitutional functionaries, who face removal proceedings, often resign to avoid removal/ impeachment. By doing so, they also ensure that they continue to enjoy the perks and facilities attached to their former offices. As per the petitioner, there is a general perception among citizens that constitutional functionaries resign to frustrate proceedings that could lead to their removal, but continue to receive the benefits attached to their offices even after stepping down. Such a practice is contrary to the rule of law, which forms part of the basic structure of the Constitution, it was submitted. In case of non-Constitutional functionaries, there are specific rules which do not permit such functionaries to resign if they are facing any departmental proceedings, the plea said. The position of Constitutional functionaries should be much higher than non-Constitutional functionaries and they must demonstrate probity in public life by completing their tenure and, if required, facing the proceedings of removal like any other employee working for the nation, it was contended. Hence, it was submitted that any provision which makes a Constitutional functionary entitled to perks, amenities and facilities even after resignation (tendered to avoid removal) should be declared as unconstitutional. Advocates Sangramsingh R Bhonsle, Pushkara A Bhonsle, Sneha S Bhonsle, Sanmitra YP, Shruti Sharma and Bhramjyot Singh represented the petitioner. The 17-year-old accused, the son of an additional district judge, was driving a Mercedes-Benz car when he hit a two-wheeler in Kochi's Cheranalloor in the early hours of October 25, killing the rider Jayabalakrishnan. A Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) on October 26 granted the accused teenager bail. Ernakulam Additional District and Sessions Judge Kavitha Gangadharan today dismissed appeals filed by the State and Jayabalakrishnan's relatives against the JJB's decision. items.summary: A Delhi court on Thursday directed that Delhi Police should not take any coercive action against Congress Member of Parliament (MP) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) professor A Bimol Akoijam in connection with the sexual harassment case against him. Several students have levelled allegations of sexual harassment against Akoijam, pursuant to which the Delhi Police registered a first information report (FIR) for offences of sexual harassment under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Special Judge Digvinay Singh of the Rouse Avenue Courts said that seven days' notice must be given to Akoijam if his arrest is required. The court noted that Akoijam has clear antecedents and that he has been cooperating in the investigation. It added that the investigation is ongoing and victims' statements have yet to be recorded because the JNU administration has not provided their names and details. Further, Judge Singh said that in case of non-cooperation in the probe, Delhi Police is at liberty to approach the court for necessary directions. Akoijam's counsel told the Court today that he had joined the probe and has been cooperating. Meanwhile, the public prosecutor informed the judge that notice was issued to JNU to provide information and details of complainants against Akoijam and that police will speak to them. Earlier, Akoijam was dismissed from JNU with immediate effect on October 9, following an inquiry into allegations of sexual harassment. However, On November 2, the Delhi High Court stayed his termination from service after Akoijam challenged the university's action. Akoijam has denied the allegations levelled against him. He has maintained that the allegations are politically motivated. The Congress MP had been associated with JNU’s Centre for the Study of Social Systems under the School of Social Sciences.

items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday said that laws that penalise having more than two children have lost their relevance since the fear of overpopulation has crumbled due to demographic changes in the past few decades as seen in the fall in fertility rate from 3 to 1.9 [ Mangala Bhimrao Ingle v. The Additional Commissioner, Amravati Division & Ors] Hence, the bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe said that a law excluding persons from contesting elections on the ground of having more than two children violates reproductive autonomy under Article 21 of the Constitution. "We are of the strong opinion that laws that penalise having more than two children have lost their relevance. The foundation of such laws, that is, the fear of overpopulation, has crumbled due to demographic changes in the past few decades. We have explained how, since 2003, when Javed v State of Haryana upheld such laws, India’s total fertility rate has fallen from 3 to 1.9," the Court observed. Pertinently, the Court referred the issue to a larger bench to decide on the validity of such a provision. items.title: Supreme Court upholds power of State legislatures to impose additional levy on sales tax
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday upheld the power of State legislatures to impose additional tax, surcharge or cess calculated on existing sales or purchase tax. A seven-judge Constitution Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices KV Viswanathan , SVN Bhatti , Joymalya Bagchi , NV Anjaria , Arun Palli and V Mohana delivered the judgment. The legal question was referred to a larger bench nearly 27 years ago. The Court said that the statutes under which the levies were imposed have since been substituted or replaced. Therefore, it added, the question did not survive for adjudication. "The question referred to is of no practical significance and now academic. Consequently, the question referred to does not survive for adjudication by a seven-judge Bench, and the reference has to be answered accordingly," the Court said. The decision means that the top court has approved the five-judge decision of S Kodar v. State of Kerala, in which additional sales tax was upheld and the contention that the levy was effectively a tax on income was rejected. "We have clarified that the case clearly held that an additional tax or surcharge computed as a percentage of the sales tax payable is an enhancement of the rate of sales tax and a tax on the sale or purchase of goods within Entry 54 of List II, as it then stood. That decision continues to hold the field," the Court ruled today. The Court added that the question of the legislative competence of the State legislature to levy the impugned surcharge itself shall be governed by the law declared in S Kodar . items.title: Karnataka High Court allows BJP MLA’s plea to disband additional land committee headed by Congress leader
items.summary: Public office cannot be treated as a consolation prize for a defeated politician, said the Karnataka High Court recently while quashing a notification that set up an additional land regularisation committee in Byndoor headed by a Congress leader who had lost the 2023 Assembly election [ Gururaj Gantihole v State of Karnataka ]. A Division Bench of Justices DK Singh and H Shanthi Bhushan found that the State had constituted the committee, with Congress leader K Gopal Poojary as its Chairman, without recording any opinion on the need for such an additional committee under Section 94-A(2-A) of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act, 1964. The Court observed that the committee appeared to have been constituted on the strength of requests by Poojary, made after his Assembly poll defeat. The notification constituting the additional committee had also adopted the team he had proposed, it noted. Criticising this approach of allowing defeated politicians to acquire power through a backdoor route, the Court said, "A personal request, political influence or the desire to rehabilitate a leader who has lost political ground cannot, by itself, furnish a justification for creating an additional position or arrangement. The circumstances suggest an attempt to secure a position of authority through an indirect route and to regain power through a back-door route, rather than to address any genuine public necessity." It warned that the State must remain about considerations of personal political advancement and ensure that its decisions are guided by public interest and genuine administrative necessity, not attempts to accommodate an individual’s desire to regain lost authority. "The desire of an individual to cling on to power cannot be permitted to dictate the course of public administration. items.summary: The Kerala High Court has reiterated that political activities like dharna, hunger strikes and other practices like Satyagraha have no place in a constitutional democracy, much less in academic institutions [ Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit v Archana PS & Ors. ]. items.summary: The Delhi High Court, a preferred forum for Intellectual Property (IP) disputes, has now questioned the practice of litigants filing IP suits before it based on the most insignificant connection with the national capital [ABD Maestro Private Limited v Great Galleon Ventures Ltd + Connected matters] . In a 246-page judgment delivered on November 3, Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav also took a dim view of the High Court entertaining such IP suits despite having little connection to the national capital. items.title: Karnataka High Court initiates suo motu case on violence against lawyers; seeks report from State
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday initiated a suo motu case to examine the increasing incidents of violence, assaults, threats and murders of advocates across the State and the need to ensure adequate protection to members of the legal fraternity. A Division Bench of Justice DK Singh and Justice H Shanti Bhushan directed the High Court registry to register a case as public interest litigation (PIL) following representations by the Advocates Association, Bengaluru (AAB), and the Karnataka State Bar Council (KSBC), highlighting the recent murders of advocates Sriram V and Manjunath, and the alleged attempt to murder Senior Advocate Venkataramanappa Sannakki. “An attack upon an advocate, particularly one resulting in the loss of life, cannot be viewed as an isolated incident, since it also affects the independence of the Bar and the administration of justice,” the Court said. Justice DK Singh and Justice H Shanthi Bhushan The Bench emphasised that advocates are officers of the Court and partners in the administration of justice, and their safety, dignity and professional independence are matters of considerable importance. The Court observed that advocates must be able to represent their clients fearlessly without apprehension of physical harm, threats or intimidation. The High Court directed the State government to examine the necessity of strengthening the existing statutory framework relating to the protection and welfare of advocates, including the Advocates Protection Act. The State has been asked to place before the Court its response on the legislative and administrative measures proposed to strengthen the existing law. The Bench noted that the increasing incidents of threats, assaults, intimidation and violence against advocates call for an examination of whether the existing statutory provisions provide adequate protection. “The concerns expressed by the Bar cannot be addressed merely by issuing assurances. Appropriate legislative and administrative measures, supported by an effective mechanism for implementation, are required,” the Court said. The High Court also took note of allegations that police stations in several instances were functioning as parallel courts by entertaining civil disputes between private parties and attempting to settle them. The Court observed that police stations cannot be converted into forums for adjudicating civil rights or settling disputes relating to property, possession, contractual obligations or other civil claims

items.title: Supreme Court says 24-hour arrest deadline begins when person is detained
items.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that the 24-hour deadline for producing an arrested person before a magistrate begins from the moment their liberty is curtailed, and not from the time the police formally record the arrest. A bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar held that excluding the period of detention before a formal arrest from the 24-hour deadline would violate Article 22(2) of the Constitution. The ruling came in appeals filed by four people challenging the Tripura High Court's rejection of their bail pleas in a case under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. The four accused were detained on September 29, 2025, at around 2 pm during a search and seizure operation. However, the police formally recorded their arrest only at 11 am the following day. The Supreme Court held that they should have been produced before a magistrate within 24 hours of their detention on September 29. According to a LiveLaw report, the court found that the accused had been kept in custody for around 18 hours without judicial oversight, violating their constitutional rights. It consequently ordered their immediate release. "Article 22(2) does not sanction exclusion of the time taken for inquiry or investigation before the arresting authority could effect arrest of the detainee," the bench observed. The court clarified that the only period that can be excluded while calculating the 24-hour deadline is the time required to travel from the place of arrest to the magistrate's court. It rejected the argument that detention before a formal arrest should be treated differently, observing that fundamental rights cannot be temporarily suspended during an investigation. The bench also disapproved of earlier rulings by the Orissa High Court in Aryaman Pattanaik, the Kerala High Court in Arun K Thomas and the Madras High Court in Kannan, which had allowed pre-arrest detention to be excluded from the 24-hour calculation. It held that these judgments did not lay down the correct position of law under Article 22(2). The Supreme Court, however, approved the Kerala High Court's ruling in Biswajith Mandal, which held that the 24-hour period begins when a person's liberty is effectively curtailed rather than when the formal arrest is recorded. The bench also issued directions to magistrates, asking them to record the actual date and time from which an accused person's liberty was curtailed when they are produced before them. items.title: Kavin caste killing: SC upholds quashing of chargesheet against accused’s cop parents
items.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed an appeal by the Tamil Nadu Crime Branch Crime Investigation Department (CB-CID) challenging a Madras High Court order to quash the chargesheet against two accused in the honour killing of Dalit techie C Kavin Selvaganesh. In September, the Madras High Court had quashed the chargesheet against the first accused, Surjith’s parents, Saravanan and Krishnakumari, both of whom are police officers. According to reports, the apex court has also criticised the state government's handling of the case. Kavin was hacked to death on July 27, 2025, at Tirunelveli’s KTC Nagar. He hailed from Arumugamangalam in Thoothukudi district and was in a relationship with a Thevar woman (Other Backward Class). Surjith, her brother, allegedly killed Kavin because he opposed the inter-caste relationship. The case was transferred to the CB-CID after it emerged that Surjith’s parents, Saravanan and Krishnakumari, were police officers and were named as accused. Both are sub-inspectors in the Tamil Nadu Special Police Force and were suspended from service following the murder. The CB-CID filed an 800-page chargesheet in October before the II Additional District Court for SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act cases in Tirunelveli, alleging that Saravanan and Krishnakumari had known about their daughter’s relationship with Kavin since 2016 or 2017. The chargesheet also alleged that Saravanan tried to dissuade his daughter and even spoke to Kavin over the phone sometime in 2018 or 2019. Further, the chargesheet accused Krishnakumari of contacting Kavin’s mother and warning her against the relationship. The Madras High Court, however, cited insufficient evidence and quashed the chargesheet. In October, the High Court also granted conditional bail to the fourth accused, Jayapal.

items.title: When journalism leaks into art: Interview with musician-journalist Carl La’Frenais
items.summary: Two people are on an unknown terrace, lying with their hands behind their heads and gazing at the night sky, missing the stars because they are too immersed in their conversation and laughing at a joke. Carl La’Frenais listens as I describe this image that flowed into my mind when his song ‘Happy Place’ was played. He laughs and then shares the real story behind it, which unsurprisingly lacks a terrace, the night sky, and the joke, but has the comforting presence of two people watching the sea together. The Fort Kochi beach is where Carl used to go early in the mornings to let his mind float before a busy day as a journalist began. Every morning, he would see an old man cycle to the beach and watch the sea, much like Carl, in total silence. Once, Carl asked him about it, and he said it was his happy place. He used to come there with his wife, but she was no longer with him, and he wanted to relive those memories and remember her every single day. “He said the visit was like going back to his happy place,” Carl says, in a brief chat about his new extended play (EP), which contains ‘Happy Place’ and three other songs, all of which are tributes to his hometown, Fort Kochi. The EP is named after the Kochi pincode, 682001. Song list on the EP Carl’s love for Kochi was much publicised in the past few days, not so much for the EP as for a video he released, to debunk a north Indian vlogger’s derogatory and communal accusations about Kochi. “It was not spontaneous. [Initially] I didn’t want to react to it, because I had spoken to the owner of Kashi Art Gallery [which the vlogger targets] and the artist related to the issue, and they said let’s let it go. But I got calls from news agencies and I thought I should address this before saying anything to anyone,” Carl says. View this post on Instagram Carl has an Instagram page full of videos, mostly reactions to current issues, that he likes to keep separate from his music. However, his job as a journalist does not really allow that anymore, and the stories he witnesses on the ground – most recently the student protests in Delhi – leak into his art. “The new stuff that I am writing, in terms of lyrics, is very much influenced by what I am seeing on the ground, and around me, on the news and in person. Not this EP, as it was written a few years ago. It is normal when you are an artist. You write about things you care about, that’s always on your mind,” he says.
